text:
sana: Heads up — after the netpol cleanup this morning we're seeing intermittent KV-sync/RDMA failures between GPU pods across AZs. Symptoms: slow reconnects, packet loss on large frames. Anyone tracking this?

mike: Which change? link to PR? any logs?

sana: PR was merged ~2043009000, changes to namespace egress selectors. Quick log from the gpu-proxy pod when handshake fails:
```
[rdma] ib_connect(): qp state error: retries exhausted, ret=-110
RDMA: qp 0x7f4faec, conn timed out
kv-sync: handshake failed: EPROTO
```

irina: I merged the cleanup — we changed the egress rule to be AZ-aware but accidentally used a podSelector-only rule in the namespace policy. That ends up blocking inter-namespace traffic when the destination pod is labeled but in a different namespace (svc mesh uses namespaceSelector elsewhere). Snippet of the problematic bit:
```
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: { name: allow-egress-gpu-proxy }
spec:
  podSelector: { matchLabels: { role: gpu-proxy } }
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
    - to:
        - podSelector: { matchLabels: { role: kv-server } }
      ports: [{ protocol: TCP, port: 2333 }]
# missing namespaceSelector -> drops cross-namespace pod traffic
```
jamie: Repro steps I ran: from pod in az-b to pod in az-a with MTU=9000 path:
```
$ ping -M do -s 8972 <peer-ip>
PING ...: sendmsg: Message too long
---
Fragmentation required, outbound fails only when using DF bit
```
jamie: So it's a combination: netpol denies egress to the cross-namespace pod endpoint (because we matched only on podSelector), and large-frame RDMA/KV traffic hits DF/MTU and can't fallback, causing handshake timeouts.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: merged PR #3421 by irina to infra/netpols — label cleanup applied to namespaces (2043009123).

alyssa: Short-term mitigation: add an explicit egress rule allowing podCIDR/namespaces for gpu-proxy traffic or annotate the namespace to allow intra-az kv-sync. Example patch:
```
kubectl patch networkpolicy allow-egress-gpu-proxy -n gpu -p '{"spec": {"egress": [{"to": [{"namespaceSelector": {"matchLabels": {"redwood-az": "az-a"}}, {"podSelector":{"matchLabels":{"role":"kv-server"}}], "ports": [{"protocol":"TCP","port":2333}] }]}}'
```
mike: Observed impact if we leave it: KV sync latency x3, GPU slice requeues -> ~40% throughput drop on training jobs in mixed-AZ clusters. Cost: extra GPU-hours and retries.

sana: Can eng-sre patch this ASAP and monitor KV latency for 30m? I'll open a follow-up runbook. @jamie can you coordinate the patch and rollbacks? :pray:

jamie: On it — will apply allow rule to affected namespaces now, watch conntrack, rdma handshakes, and restore the stricter selector after we add namespaceSelector-based rules. Commands I'll run:
```
kubectl apply -f fixes/egress-allow-az.yaml -n gpu
kubectl get pods -n gpu -l role=kv-server -o wide
watch -n 5 'ss -tn state established | grep 2333'
```

sana: Thanks. We'll do a short postmortem after. Note to team: avoid podSelector-only egress rules when mesh cross-namespace flows are required (especially for RDMA/MTU-sensitive traffic).
